title: Hearts 8-0 Dundee: Eight Goals and a Message to the League
body:
Hearts dismantled Dundee 8-0 at Dens Park, and they did it against a side that had been reduced to ten men [S1][S2]. The scoreline alone would be eye-catching, but the way it was built makes it more interesting. Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré each scored twice [S1]. The rest came from other scorers, plus an own goal by Ryan Finnigan [S1].

The manager, Wouter Vrancken, called it the best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle [S1]. It also ended a run of three defeats in a row [S1]. BBC Sport framed it as a reply to a worrying week before the international break [S2]. This was the kind of game that tells you more about character than about tactics. A reply this loud also sends a message to everyone still chasing the top of the table.

Elsewhere in the round, Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1, and Steven Pressley said he was embarrassed and apologised [S1]. Rangers beat Motherwell 2-1 [S1].

The big question is whether this was a one-off or a sign of real recovery. A side can look like a team again on one blazing afternoon. The real test is what comes next, and a performance like this only matters if it is repeated.

The Touchline Take: file this one under unfinished business, because a side that finds its identity under pressure is one nobody wants to meet.

evidence.text: The Guardian: Scottish Premiership roundup: Dundee left reeling after 8-0 mauling by Hearts. Steven Pressley: ‘I’m embarrassed … I apologise’ Celtic 4-1 St Mirren; Rangers 2-1 Motherwell. Wouter Vrancken said Hearts ’ remarkable 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle. Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

BBC Sport: 'They looked like a team again' - Hearts roar back with Dundee demolition. After a worrying week before the international break, Hearts respond is style by thrashing Dundee 8-0 at Dens Park.
